 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Portland Trail Blazers continue their six-game trip Thursday with a visit to the Milwaukee Bucks at 5 p.m.
 The game will air live on KUNP and BlazerVision.
 Here are three things we're keeping an eye on tonight:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Damian Lillard returns to Milwaukee
 The game will be a reunion for Damian Lillard , who is poised to face the Bucks for the first time since the team waived him in July 2025.
 The nine-time All-Star played two seasons in Milwaukee alongside MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo, forming one of the most feared tandems in the NBA. Lillard averaged 24.6 points, 7.0 assists and 4.5 rebounds in 131 games for the Bucks and was twice named an All-Star, but the team never advanced beyond the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs, in large part because of injuries.
 It was a career-threatening injury, of course, that ended Lillard's time there — he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon on April 27, 2025, during the first round of the playoffs, and spent last season in rehabilitation.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement So, this will be his first visit to Fiserv Forum since the night he tore his Achilles.
 Declining health may leave Blazers without key players
 Injuries are starting to mount for the Blazers (9-5), who could be without three starters and an important rotation big man against the Bucks.
 All-Star forward Deni Avdija missed Tuesday night's loss against the Minnesota Timberwolves with left foot inflammation and soreness and is listed as questionable tonight. Likewise, forward Toumani Camara has surfaced on the Blazers' injury report with abdominal soreness.
 The Blazers' defensive anchor — who has played in 96 consecutive games — evidently suffered the ailment during the Blazers' back-to-back in Minneapolis.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What's more, the Blazers are resting backup center Robert Williams III against the Bucks, so he has been ruled out. The trio of rotation players joins a crowded injury list that also includes four Blazers who will not play: Ja Morant (left hamstring strain), Shaedon Sharpe (right meniscus surgery), Vit Krejci (left ankle fracture) and Chris Youngblood (bruised right heel).

 Opportunity for Jayson Kent
 Avdija's injury has created an unexpected opportunity for Jayson Kent , and the two-way player could see an expanded role in the wake of the Blazers' injuries.
 The 6-foot-8 forward made his first NBA start — in his 10th career game — Tuesday at Minneapolis, and held his own, recording eight points, three rebounds and two steals, while making 3 of 6 shots, in 27 minutes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It was a storybook moment for the second-year player, who landed with the organization via a G League local tryout. Kent played well enough during last fall's tryout to earn a roster spot with the Rip City Remix, then played well enough in the G League to land a two-way contract in March with the Blazers.
 He's just the 10th player in league history to start an NBA game after participating in a G League local tryout.
